lesson.title: Learn React useEffect Hook
lesson.goal: learn the React useEffect hook: run side effects on mount and on state changes, and clean them up

steps.title: Set up project and counter
steps.instructions: Create a Vite React project (npm create vite@latest, React template), render MyComponent in src/App.jsx, and run npm run dev. In src/MyComponent.jsx, import useState and useEffect, add count state, and render an Add button.

targets.caption: Import hooks, declare count state, and render the Add button

explanations.topic: What useEffect does and when it runs
useEffect syntax and dependency array options
Common use cases and mounting vs unmounting

hints: Start by scaffolding the app with npm create vite@latest my-react-app -- --template react, installing dependencies, and rendering <MyComponent /> inside App.jsx.
Import both useState and useEffect from "react" on line 1 of src/MyComponent.jsx.
Use const [count, setCount] = useState(0); and update it inside addCount with setCount(c => c + 1).
common_mistakes: Forgetting to render <MyComponent /> and export it from src/MyComponent.jsx.
Calling addCount() with parentheses in onClick={addCount()} instead of passing the function reference.
Updating count directly instead of calling setCount(c => c + 1).
steps.code:
import React, {useState, useEffect} from "react"; function MyComponent() { const [count, setCount] = useState(0); function addCount(){ setCount(c => c + 1); } return (<>

Count: {count}

); } export default MyComponent;

steps.title: Update document title on render
steps.instructions: Call useEffect near the top of MyComponent with an arrow function that sets document.title using count. Click Add in the browser and verify the tab title updates on every re-render.

targets.caption: Add useEffect without dependencies to run after every re-render

hints: Place useEffect(() => { ... }); above addCount inside MyComponent.
Use template literals with backticks so ${count} interpolates into document.title.
Write: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; });
common_mistakes: Using single or double quotes instead of backticks (`) for the template string `Count: ${count}`.
Placing useEffect inside a nested handler or conditional instead of the top level of the component.

steps.title: Run useEffect only on mount
steps.instructions: In src/MyComponent.jsx pass an empty array [] as the second argument to useEffect so it runs only once on mount. Click Add to confirm the document title no longer updates on re-renders.

targets.caption: Pass an empty dependency array to run the effect only on mount

hints: What second argument tells React that this effect has no dependencies?
Add a comma after the callback function's closing brace and pass [].
Update the hook call to end with }, []);
common_mistakes: Omitting the comma between the callback function and the dependency array.
Passing [] inside the arrow function body instead of as the second argument to useEffect.

steps.title: Add count dependency and Subtract button
steps.instructions: Add count to the useEffect dependency array so the title updates on mount and when count changes. Create a subtractCount function and a Subtract button.

targets.caption: Watch count in the dependency array and add a Subtract handler

hints: Put count inside the square brackets at the end of useEffect.
Duplicate addCount, rename it to subtractCount, and use c => c - 1.
Render <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button> right below the Add button.
common_mistakes: Leaving the dependency array empty [] and wondering why the tab title stops updating.
Forgetting to change + 1 to - 1 in subtractCount.
steps.code: useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count}`; }, [count]); function subtractCount(){ setCount(c => c - 1); } <button onClick={subtractCount}>Subtract</button>

steps.title: Add color state and dependency
steps.instructions: Add a color state initialized to "green", a Change Color button and style={{color: color}} on the paragraph. Include color in document.title and in the useEffect dependency array.

targets.caption: Add color to the dependency array so color toggles also update the title

explanations.topic: Benefits of useEffect for organization and conditional execution
Returning a cleanup function from useEffect

hints: Declare const [color, setColor] = useState("green"); below the count state.
In JSX, inline styles take an object inside curly braces: style={{color: color}}.
Add ${color} to the title template string and pass [count, color] as the dependency array.
common_mistakes: Using single curly braces style={color: color} instead of double curly braces style={{color: color}}.
Including ${color} in document.title without adding color to the dependency array, causing stale titles on color changes.
steps.code:
const [color, setColor] = useState("green"); useEffect(() => { document.title = `Count: ${count} ${color}`; }, [count, color]); function changeColor(){ setColor(c => c === "green" ? "red" : "green"); }

Count: {count}

steps.title: Track window dimensions in state
steps.instructions: Reset MyComponent to track width and height state initialized from window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight. Display both dimensions in paragraphs and define a handleResize function that updates them.

targets.caption: Read window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight into state

hints: Initialize width and height using window.innerWidth and window.innerHeight inside useState(...).
Inside handleResize, call setWidth(window.innerWidth) and setHeight(window.innerHeight).

Render

Window Width: {width}px

and

Window Height: {height}px

.
common_mistakes: Misspelling innerWidth or innerHeight with incorrect capitalization.
Calling setWidth inside useState or forgetting to create the handleResize updater.
steps.code:
const [width, setWidth] = useState(window.innerWidth); const [height, setHeight] = useState(window.innerHeight); function handleResize(){ setWidth(window.innerWidth); setHeight(window.innerHeight); } return (<>

Window Width: {width}px

Window Height: {height}px

);

steps.title: Register resize listener on mount
steps.instructions: Inside a useEffect with an empty dependency array, call window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) and console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"). Resize the window and check DevTools that it logs only once.

targets.caption: Attach the resize event listener only once on component mount

explanations.topic: Why React StrictMode invokes useEffect twice in development

hints: Avoid calling window.addEventListener directly in the component body because it adds a new listener on every re-render.
Wrap window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize) in useEffect(() => { ... }, []);.
Open browser DevTools Console and resize the window to confirm "EVENT LISTENER ADDED" does not repeat on every resize.
common_mistakes: Calling window.addEventListener outside useEffect, flooding the browser with thousands of listeners.
Passing handleResize() with parentheses instead of passing the function reference handleResize.
steps.code: useEffect(() => { window.addEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER ADDED"); }, []);

steps.title: Clean up event listener on unmount
steps.instructions: Return a cleanup arrow function from the resize useEffect that calls window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize) and logs "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED". Reload and check the console to see the cleanup run in StrictMode.

targets.caption: Return a cleanup function to remove the listener when unmounting

hints: How do you tell useEffect to run cleanup code when a component unmounts?
At the bottom of the useEffect callback, return a function: return () => { ... }.
Inside that returned function, call window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); and log "EVENT LISTENER REMOVED".
common_mistakes: Calling window.removeEventListener directly inside useEffect instead of inside a returned cleanup function.
Passing a different function reference to removeEventListener than the one passed to addEventListener.
steps.code: return () => { window.removeEventListener("resize", handleResize); console.log("EVENT LISTENER REMOVED"); }

steps.title: Add second useEffect for title
steps.instructions: Add a second useEffect that sets document.title to `Size: ${width} x ${height}` with [width, height] as dependencies. Resize the window and verify the tab title updates.

targets.caption: Add a second useEffect hook focused on updating document.title

hints: A single React component can contain multiple useEffect hooks for separate concerns.
Create another useEffect(() => { ... }, [width, height]); below the first one.
Assign document.title = `Size: ${width} x ${height}`; inside the second useEffect.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to include both width and height in the dependency array.
Nesting the second useEffect inside the first useEffect instead of placing it at the top level of MyComponent.
